source.title: Function Norms and Regularization in Deep Networks
source.authors: A. Triki; Maxim Berman; Matthew B. Blaschko

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares dropout with other regularization methods on MNIST and reports held-out performance, using its own experiments rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper cites work on random-label fitting, batch size, sharpness, and generalization, but reports no new results on those findings. It reports dropout comparisons in figures; numerical values are figure-only, and the text does not explicitly state whether dropout alone improves over no dropout.
record.test_reason: The MNIST experiments compare configurations with and without dropout. Section 5.2 explicitly reports an incremental benefit from combining dropout with function-norm regularization, although the supplied figure text cannot establish dropout-only effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The authors conclude that their function-norm regularizers improve performance over popular regularization strategies. They also tentatively report that combining their regularization with dropout improves performance further; they do not establish a textual dropout-only versus no-dropout conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a proposed weighted function-norm regularizer against dropout and other methods; it does not reproduce the cited dropout studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported regularization comparisons vary the regularization batch size and sampling distribution. The authors state that larger regularization batches can reach higher performance but show higher variance; two Gaussian sampling settings caused divergence and random performance. These are properties of their proposed regularizer, not dropout effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Weighted function-norm regularization outperforms competing regularizers; its performance depends on its sampling distribution and regularization batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sampling-based function-norm regularization can improve held-out performance in low-data settings.

record.code_released: Source code will be released at the time of publication.
record.problems: The dropout comparisons are presented as curves in figures without numerical values in the text. The paper does not explicitly state whether dropout alone improves over the no-dropout condition, so the effect named by V6 cannot be determined from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted. Dropout comparisons appear in Figures 2, 3, and 8, but the text does not report an explicit dropout-versus-no-dropout outcome; values are figure-only.

untested.parts: No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No training-batch comparison under fixed epoch budgets; regularization sampling batches are a different variable.

Dropout-only versus no-dropout outcomes cannot be determined from the supplied figure text. Excessive dropout, training-set-size dependence, and removing dropout with weight decay under augmentation are not established.
No magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap comparison.

missing.what: A qualitative row for adding dropout to function-norm regularization: the authors report further performance improvement. The record's explanation for omitting rows overlooks this explicit textual incremental-dropout result. Effect size and uncertainty cannot be recovered.

record.verdict_notes: No rows were supplied. Figure legends and axis values do not reveal curve ordering, so no numerical dropout effects are inferred. The qualitative verdict rests on the explicit Section 5.2 statement.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization are cited, not tested.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold results.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD on the main models.
No comparison of training batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.

The study compares dropout-containing configurations and dropout-only configurations in figures, but does not state a dropout versus no-dropout effect in text. Figure-only curves do not support a reliable row-level effect or verdict.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: LeNet on 100 MNIST training examples, adding dropout to weighted function-norm regularization with weight decay.
relationships.reason: Section 5.2 qualitatively reports further improvement when dropout is added, qualifying V6's exclusion of very small training sets. This tentative textual result has no extracted row or numerical effect size.
relationships.display_finding: Adding dropout reportedly further improved performance under the combined regularization recipe. This tentative comparison has not been verified or quantified.
